# shopify_discount_bxgy (Resource)

A buy X get Y discount: customers who buy a quantity or an amount of some items get a quantity of other items at a percentage or an amount off, as a code discount (`code` set) or an automatic one (`code` unset). **Volatile, usually a poor fit for Terraform:** promotions are created, changed and ended in the admin by marketing, and every admin edit to a managed attribute is reverted on the next apply. Destroying a discount deletes it; orders keep their discount applications, but a recreated discount counts its uses from zero. Bulk codes, tags, subscription settings and app discounts are not managed. Generated config holds product, collection, segment and market GIDs, which tie it to the store: replace them with references. An existing discount with the same code, or an automatic one with the same title, needs `adopt_existing = true`; destroy then leaves it in place. Import with `code/<code>` or `automatic/<title>`. A selection of more than 250 items per list is not read yet.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "shopify_collection" "pflegehilfsmittel" {
  handle = "pflegehilfsmittel"
  title  = "Pflegehilfsmittel"
}

# Automatic discount: buy 2 items of the collection, get 1 of them free (at most once per order).
resource "shopify_discount_bxgy" "zwei_fuer_eins" {
  title                = "2 kaufen, 1 gratis"
  uses_per_order_limit = 1

  customer_buys = {
    quantity = 2
    items    = { collection_ids = [shopify_collection.pflegehilfsmittel.id] }
  }
  customer_gets = {
    quantity   = 1
    percentage = 1
    items      = { collection_ids = [shopify_collection.pflegehilfsmittel.id] }
  }
}

# Code discount: spend 30 € on the collection, get 2 of its items 5 € off each. Unset attributes stay with the admin.
resource "shopify_discount_bxgy" "bonus" {
  title = "Bonus"
  code  = "BONUS5"

  customer_buys = {
    amount = "30.00"
    items  = { collection_ids = [shopify_collection.pflegehilfsmittel.id] }
  }
  customer_gets = {
    quantity = 2
    amount   = "5.00"
    items    = { collection_ids = [shopify_collection.pflegehilfsmittel.id] }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `customer_buys` (Attributes) What the customer buys: `items` and exactly one of `quantity` or `amount`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_buys))
- `customer_gets` (Attributes) What the customer gets: `items`, the `quantity` that is discounted and exactly one of `percentage` or `amount`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_gets))
- `title` (String) The discount's name in the admin and at checkout. Unique among automatic discounts; code discounts may share titles.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing discount with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `applies_once_per_customer` (Boolean) Whether each customer can use the code only once. Code discounts only. Unset means unmanaged.
- `code` (String) The code customers enter; unset makes an automatic discount. Unique per shop, ignoring case; Shopify keeps the case as given. Changing the code renames it in place, but setting or removing it replaces the discount, which restarts its usage count. Discounts with several codes can be imported by any of them, but their code can't be changed here.
- `combines_with` (Attributes) Which other discount classes it combines with. All `false` when created without it. Unset means unmanaged. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--combines_with))
- `context` (Attributes) Who can use the discount: exactly one of `all`, `customer_segment_ids` or `market_ids`. A code discount created without it is open to all buyers. Reference `shopify_customer_segment` IDs: deleting a discount's only segment expires the discount and resets it to all buyers, and the reference makes Terraform update the discount first. A discount for individual customers, or with a context Shopify doesn't describe, reads as null and can't be managed here. Unset means unmanaged. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--context))
- `ends_at` (String) When the discount ends, as an RFC 3339 time; null means no end. Setting it in the past ends the discount. An end date set in the admin can't be removed here: set a far end date instead. Unset means unmanaged.
- `starts_at` (String) When the discount starts, as an RFC 3339 time such as `2026-11-01T00:00:00+01:00`. Shopify returns UTC; the instant is compared, so the configured spelling stays. Created as now when unset. Unset means unmanaged.
- `usage_limit` (Number) How often the code can be used in total; null means unlimited. Code discounts only. A limit set in the admin can't be removed here: set a high limit instead. Unset means unmanaged.
- `uses_per_order_limit` (Number) How often the discount can apply to one order. A limit set in the admin can't be removed here: set a high one instead. Unset means unmanaged.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `DiscountCodeNode` or `DiscountAutomaticNode` GID.
- `status` (String) `ACTIVE`, `SCHEDULED` or `EXPIRED`, from the dates.

<a id="nestedatt--customer_buys"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_buys`

Required:

- `items` (Attributes) The items the customer buys: `product_ids` and/or `variant_ids`, or `collection_ids`. Shopify refuses all items here. Changes are written as additions and removals against the live selection. A selection whose items are all gone (for example deleted products) reads as `product_ids = []` or `collection_ids = []`; Shopify rejects creating such a discount, and any update to it unless the same change adds items. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_buys--items))

Optional:

- `amount` (String) Purchase amount of the items in the shop currency, as a decimal string. Compared numerically, so `"30"` matches Shopify's `"30.0"`.
- `quantity` (Number) Number of items the customer buys.

<a id="nestedatt--customer_buys--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_buys.items`

Optional:

- `collection_ids` (Set of String) Collection GIDs; reference `shopify_collection` IDs.
- `product_ids` (Set of String) Product GIDs; reference `shopify_product` IDs.
- `variant_ids` (Set of String) Product variant GIDs.



<a id="nestedatt--customer_gets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_gets`

Required:

- `items` (Attributes) The items the customer gets: `product_ids` and/or `variant_ids`, or `collection_ids`. Shopify refuses all items here. Changes are written as additions and removals against the live selection. A selection whose items are all gone (for example deleted products) reads as `product_ids = []` or `collection_ids = []`; Shopify rejects creating such a discount, and any update to it unless the same change adds items. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_gets--items))
- `quantity` (Number) Number of items that get the discount.

Optional:

- `amount` (String) A fixed amount off each discounted item in the shop currency, as a decimal string. Compared numerically.
- `percentage` (Number) A fraction greater than 0 and at most 1 off each discounted item, such as `1` for free.

<a id="nestedatt--customer_gets--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_gets.items`

Optional:

- `collection_ids` (Set of String) Collection GIDs; reference `shopify_collection` IDs.
- `product_ids` (Set of String) Product GIDs; reference `shopify_product` IDs.
- `variant_ids` (Set of String) Product variant GIDs.



<a id="nestedatt--combines_with"></a>
### Nested Schema for `combines_with`

Optional:

- `order_discounts` (Boolean) Whether it combines with order discounts. Defaults to `false` when `combines_with` is set.
- `product_discounts` (Boolean) Whether it combines with product discounts. Defaults to `false` when `combines_with` is set.
- `shipping_discounts` (Boolean) Whether it combines with shipping discounts. Defaults to `false` when `combines_with` is set.


<a id="nestedatt--context"></a>
### Nested Schema for `context`

Optional:

- `all` (Boolean) All buyers. Must be `true`.
- `customer_segment_ids` (Set of String) Customer segment GIDs.
- `market_ids` (Set of String) Market GIDs; reference `shopify_market` IDs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# code/<code> for a code discount, automatic/<title> for an automatic one
terraform import shopify_discount_bxgy.bonus code/BONUS5
terraform import shopify_discount_bxgy.zwei_fuer_eins "automatic/2 kaufen, 1 gratis"
```
